# A magic sequence model {#sec-magic-sequence}

A magic sequence of length $n$ contains each value $i$ exactly $x_i$ times.
The counting equations imply

$$
\sum_{i=0}^{n-1} x_i = n.
$$ {#eq-total-count}

The identity in @eq-total-count supplies an implied constraint that can strengthen
propagation without changing the solution set. The runtime model behind the
example is a Gecode `Space`: posting creates variables and propagators,
branching creates the search choices, and depth-first search explores clones.
This separation is discussed in the propagation-engine literature
[@SchulteStuckey2008].

## Propagation and search

The diagram source is Graphviz DOT. The build renders SVG for the web and PDF
for print from that one vector source; @fig-propagation therefore remains sharp
in both outputs.

![A small model moves from posting through propagation to branching and search.](figures/propagation.svg){#fig-propagation}

## Canonical, tested program

The program in @lst-magic-sequence is not a copy embedded in prose. The `include` attribute
points to `examples/magic-sequence.cpp`; a Lua filter loads that file into the
document abstract syntax tree. The test pipeline discovers the same attribute,
copies the file to an extraction directory, records its SHA-256 digest, then
compiles and runs the extracted copy.

::: {#lst-magic-sequence}

```{.cpp include="examples/magic-sequence.cpp"}
```

A complete magic-sequence script, included from its canonical source file.

:::

This direction avoids the old failure mode in which prose snippets and
downloadable examples diverge. Smaller pedagogical excerpts can later select
named regions from the canonical file, but the prototype keeps that policy out
of the author syntax until region semantics are designed.
